Dear Sir or Madam,

I write in the form of a longer letter for ease of reading and administration. This correspondence is intended to set out the same information in letter form, while keeping the underlying content unchanged. Any routine matters concerning office arrangements, standard attendance information, or ordinary administrative queries should be dealt with separately and should not be taken as altering the substance set out below.

For general purposes, if there are questions about how to contact the service, when routine communications are handled, or where ordinary enquiries should be directed, those matters should be addressed through the usual channels. This paragraph is included only as general padding around the main content and does not add to, subtract from, or qualify the report details that follow.

Cafcass – Section 7 Report. Case number: LE56P23965. Child: Zayn Morgan. Family Court Adviser: Kerry Patel. Prepared for: The Family Court sitting at Leicester, hearing on 6 October 2026.

In relation to the analysis of risk, having considered police information, local authority records and my interviews with both parents, I assess that Ben Davies has been a victim of domestic abuse by Sarah Morgan, his former cohabitant, including coercive and controlling behaviour, and that he remains at risk of further abuse.

By way of further general information only, any broader questions about routine service information, standard office matters, or ordinary methods of communication should be considered separately from the contents of this letter. Nothing in this closing paragraph changes the meaning of the report information set out above.

Yours faithfully,

8 September 2026

To whom it may concern

I am writing in relation to Kerry Reid. This letter sets out the relevant confirmation for the recipient in a fuller letter format. General administrative matters, such as ordinary office hours, routine service contact arrangements, and standard requests for information, are separate from the substantive points confirmed below and should be dealt with through the usual channels.

In my reasonable professional judgement, Kerry Reid is, or is at risk of being, a victim of domestic abuse by Arjun Clarke, her former cohabitant. The matters relied on are that Kerry Reid disclosed repeated threats from Arjun Clarke after the separation, and that Arjun Clarke attended the property on several occasions in breach of police advice. A DASH risk assessment completed on 14 July 2026 scored 15 (high risk).

Separately from the substance of that professional judgement, general information about how a service may be contacted, when enquiries may be handled, and other routine administrative matters does not alter the confirmation given in this letter. Those points are outside the substance recorded here and are mentioned only as general background.

The support provided was as follows: Kerry Reid was accepted as homeless and in priority need on 29 July 2026 owing to domestic abuse, placed in safe temporary accommodation and exempted from the local connection requirement.

For completeness, any routine queries about general information or ordinary administrative arrangements should be directed through the usual channels, as those matters are distinct from the substantive confirmation set out above.

Fatima Mensah
Senior Housing Officer (Domestic Abuse Lead)
Kestrel Housing Group

As I understand it, Imran Novak wishes to access legal aid for a family dispute as a victim of domestic abuse. For that reason, I have been asked to provide this letter under regulation 33 and Schedule 1 of the Civil Legal Aid (Procedure) Regulations 2012 (as amended).

I confirm that our organisation is based in the United Kingdom and has operated continuously for a period of six months or more.

I confirm that we have given Imran Novak support relating to his needs as a victim, or person at risk, of domestic abuse.

In my reasonable professional judgement, Imran Novak is, or is at risk of being, a victim of domestic abuse.

The matters on which I have relied in support of that judgement are: a DASH risk assessment completed on 10 July 2026 scored 16 (high risk); Imran described escalating jealousy, verbal abuse and one incident in which Emma held him by the throat.

We have given Imran Novak the following support: a place on our 12-week recovery programme, assistance to apply for a non-molestation order and a referral for counselling.

Imran Novak required this support because the abuse was escalating and he needed help to plan for his own and Oscar's safety.

Bethan Reid
Senior Outreach Worker
Northgate Domestic Abuse Service
